lessons: Parse category names at the final underscore; instance suffixes are not persistent tracking identities.
Use basket dimensions and orientation for containment, not a broad fixed proximity threshold.
Assign distinct baskets to distinct categories; preserve unambiguous existing category occupancy.
Normalize both supplied arm quaternions and select an arm using observed source and destination positions.
Use the calibrated contact offset with the minimum tool height; avoid unnecessarily tall lift targets.
Use bounded, single-attempt manipulation sequences and stop on unavailable perception or planning.

rationale: The correction addresses the rejected policy's broad containment test, left-arm-only motion, excessive lift height, and repeated attempts based on unstable instance names. Basket assignments and targets come only from live scene observations. The policy uses dimension-aware containment, a short approach-and-lift sequence, and distinct category destinations without modulo reuse. It stops on RPC uncertainty rather than releasing at an unknown location or retrying manipulation. Primitive completion is not treated as proof of grasping or sorting; the independent evaluator determines the outcome.
